Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Call to Order/Roll Call With Invocation & Pledge
CALL TO ORDER:  Maria Davila, Mayor

INVOCATION:  Steve Costley, Director Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer

ROLL CALL:  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

Public Hearings: None
Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to

  2
 disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including Ordinances,
Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these
items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific items be
removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

  5
 The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City

  6
 Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0.  3  TO  CONTRACT  N0.  2023-134-AC  FOR
PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  WITH  W. G. ZIMMERMAN  ENGINEERING,  INC.,  FOR
ENGINEERING  ST AFF AUGMENT  ATION

PURPOSE:  To approve Amendment  No. 3 to Contract  No. 2023-134-AC  ("Amendment  No. 3")
with W.G. Zirnmerman Engineering, Inc., ("Zirnmerman")  to continue receiving  engineering  staff
augmentation services, as well as to fully fund services provided to date.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  3 to Contract  No.  2023-134-AC  with  W.G.  Zimmerman
  Engineering,  Inc. ("Agreement")  to extend the contract  term through  June 30, 2026, to
  continue  receiving  engineering  staffing  augmentation  services, for an amount not to exceed
  $170,000;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No. 3 in a form  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  Amendment No. 3 to the Agreement is in the amount of $170,000 and it will
be funded with General Funds budgeted in salary savings. However, when appropriate, the cost
of actual services will be allocated  to chargeable  activities  such as Capital  Improvement  Program
funds, development  fee, and other.  The total revised  contract  amount is $494,311.

ANALYSIS:  Under  the Agreement,  W.G.  Zirnmerman  Engineering,  Inc.  provides  interim
engineering  staff augmentation  services  to support  the Public  Works  Department,  Engineering
Division,  in response  to ongoing  staffing  vacancies.  The contract  was originally  approved  on
September  25, 2023, and has been amended twice to extend services through  March 1, 2025, due
to the continued  need for support.  Services concluded  on April  10, 2025, following  the hiring  of a
full-time  staff member;  however,  that position  has since become vacant, once again necessitating
staff augmentation  to meet workload  and operational  demands.  Amendment  No. 3 authorizes  an
additional$l70,000  to continue services through June 30, 2026, and includes  $10,000 to fully  fund
services  previously  provided through April 10, 2025.

Amendment  No. 3 is proposed  to be funded  with  General  Funds in accordance  with  the City

  1

  8
 Council-approved  policy,  adopted  June 13, 2023.  It allows  the use of salary  savings  to fund
temporary  staffing  to minimize  disruption  to essential  services.  However,  Zirnmerman  staff will
focus primarily  on chargeable  activities  such as Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP")  support
and development  review.  While  the actual cost of these services will  be funded  with  restricted
funds, General Fund resources will only be used for non-chargeable  tasks, such as customer  service
at the Public Works counter.

BACKGROUND:  The Engineering  Division  of the Public Works Department  provides  essential
services,  including  management  of the CIP,  development  review,  plan  check,  construction
inspection,  permit  issuance,  and customer  support  at the Public  Works  counter,  among  other
responsibilities.  The Division  is currently experiencing  several vacancies,  and recruitment  for
these hard-to-fill  positions has become increasingly  challenging.

To  ensure  continuity  of  operations,  the City  maintains  a contract  with  W.G.  Zirnmerman
Engineering,  Inc. for interim staff augmentation  services. These services enable the Division  to
sustain its workload and service levels while recruitment  efforts are ongoing.

On September  26, 2023,  the City  Council  approved  the Agreement,  with  Zirnmerman  in  the
amount  of $47,311.  On March  12, 2024, the City  Council  approved  Amendment  No. 1 to the
Agreement  in the amount of $167,000  to fund services through  September 12, 2024. On November
26, 2024,  the City  Council  approved  Amendment  No. 2 to the Agreement  in the amount  of
$100,000  to extend services through  March 1, 2025. Amendment  No. 3 to the Agreement  extends
services through  June 30, 2026. The total revised contract  amount is $494,311.

Amendment  No. 3 includes  $160,000  to continue  staff augmentation  services  and an additional
$10,000  to fully  fund services provided  between  March  1, 2025, and April  10, 2025.  Under this
amendment,  services will be billed  at a rate of $120 per hour, not to exceed a total of $170,000.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  MINAGAR  &  ASSOCIATES,  INC.,  FOR
PROFESSIONAL  ENGINEERING  SERVICES  FOR  THE  CITYWIDE  ENGINEERING
AND  TRAFFIC  SURVEY  PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  736-RPT

PURPOSE:  To award  a professional  services  agreement  to Minagar  &  Associates,  Inc.,  to
prepare  a Citywide  Engineering  and Traffic  Survey  ("Project").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Minagar  & Associates,  Inc.,  for Professional  Engineering
  Services  to prepare  the Citywide  Engineering  and Traffic  Survey  Project,  City  Project  No.
  736-RPT,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $78,879; and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The Agreement  is in the amount  of $78,879  and it will  be funded  with
General  Funds  budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  0perating  Budget.

ANALYSIS:  The City's  most recent  Engineering  and Traffic  Survey  ("E&TS")  was certified  in
2011  and has been  extended  multiple  times,  allowing  the  continued  use  of radar  and  laser
enforcement  through  December  31, 2025.  However,  as of January  1, 2026,  this  E&TS  will  no
longer  be valid.  To remain  compliant  with  state law and maintain  speed enforcement  capabilities,
the City  must prepare  and certify  a new Engineering  and Traffic  Survey.

Minagar  &  Associates,  Inc.  initially  submitted  a $55,111  cost  proposal.  However,  following
discussions  and  scope  clarification  meetings,  it became  apparent  that  additional  tasks  were
necessary  to fully  achieve  the City's  objectives  and comply  with  updated  state regulations.  These
tasks include  a comprehensive  Level  of Service  ("LOS")  analysis  at all signalized  intersections,  a
signage  and pavement  marking  audit,  and enhanced  data collection  and reporting.  The consultant
agreed  to incorporate  these expanded  services,  resulting  in a revised  fee not to exceed  $78,879.
Staff reviewed  the updated  scope and pricing  and determined  them  to be fair  and reasonable  for
the level  of work  required.

  1

  13
 BACKGROUND:  The City's  street network  consists  of over 125 centerline  miles  of roadway,
including  major  arterials,  collector  streets,  and residential  streets.  Speed  limits  on major  and
collector  roadways  are established  through  an E&TS.  These limits  are enforced  by the South Gate
Police  Department  ("SGPD"),  but only  if a current,  valid  E&TS  is in place,  as required  by the
California  Vehicle  Code.

In January  2012,  Hartzog  & Crabill,  Inc. ("HCr')  prepared  a citywide  E&TS  in accordance  with
state requirements,  and it was certified  by a registered  Traffic  Engineer.  The survey  was initially
valid  for five  years after which  it qualified  for several  extensions  allowed  under  State law.  The
current  E&TS,  is valid  through  December  31, 2025.  To maintain  compliance  with  the law  and
preserve  SGPD's  ability  to enforce  speed limits  using  radar  or laser, the City  must prepare  and
adopt a new E&TS  before  the expiration  date.

Under  California  Vehicle  Code Section  40802,  an E&TS  is required  for the Police  Department  to
legally  use radar or laser devices  for speed enforcement.  An E&TS  is a study conducted  by traffic
engineers  that  evaluates  roadway  conditions,  traffic  speeds,  and  safety  data  to  determine
appropriate  speed limits.  These surveys  are initially  valid  for five years,  with  possible  extensions
to  seven  or ten  years  based  on specific  conditions.  Additionally,  Assembly  Bill  43 (AB  43),
effective  January  1, 2022,  allows  for a 'further  four-year  extension  beyond  the ten-year  limit  if the
survey  meets certain  criteria  and is certified  by a registered  Traffic  Engineer.

TASK  E - COLLECT  AVERAGE  DAILY  TRAFFIC  VOLUMES  FOR  49 SEGMENTS
The objective  of this taslc is to collect  the vehicle  volume  counts  required  to  measure  two-way

traffic  during  typical  weekday  conditions,  which  reflects  the average  daily traffic  traversing  the
segment  on a normal  basis. Counts  Unlimited  staff will deploy  multiple  field technicians  to  set

up roadway  traffic  tubes, or machine  counters,  to collect  the  average  daily traffic  counts  (ADT).
The  counter  placement  plan will be as follows:

  *  Machine  traffic volume counts  for  each roadway  segment  shall be taken  to meet  the
  following  general parameters:
  o  Scheduled  on typical school weekdays  (Tuesdays,  Wednesdays,  or Thursdays);
  o  One-day  (24 consecutive-hour)  periods  along  49  segments  for  the  weekday
  period, in no less than 15-minute  increments;
  o  For all lanes in both simultaneous  directions  of vehicular  travel;
  o  Under  good weather  conditions  with  affecting  lane closures  or detours

  *  Project  Manager  Fred Minagar  will coordinate  between  our field leads at CUI and City
  of South  Gate staff prior  to the final locating  and placement  of tubes to coincide  to  the
  extent  feasible  with  off-times  for  street  sweeping,  landscape  maintenance  activities,
  and/or  any planned  construction  work  or  other  events.

  *  Counters  shall  be  set  at  approximately  the  midpoint  of  each  roadway  segment;

  otherwise  as far  as possible  from  public  street  intersections,  private  driveways  and
  other  locations  where  vehicles  might  cross  counter  tubes  at angles  other  than  90
  degrees.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE  PURCHASE  ORDERS  FOR  THE  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY
DEPARTMENT  OF PUBLIC  WORKS  TO FtJND  BRIDGE  MAINTENANCE  SERVICES,
CITY  PROJECT  N0.  719-ST,  BRIDGE  MAINTENANCE  AND  REPAIR

PURPOSE:  To approve  purchase  orders for the Los Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Works
necessary  to arrange  for maintenance  services  on four  City-owned  bridges  and appropriate  funds
to 'fully  fund the work.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Coiu'icil  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Purchase  Orders  for  Los  Angeles  County  Public  Works  to perform  bridge
  maintenance  services  on four  city-owned  bridges,  for a cumulative  amount  of $117,020
  plus a 10%  contingency  of $12,000  for a total not to exceed the amount  of $129,020;  and
  b.  Appropriating$200,OOOfromPropositionCFundstoCIPProjectNo.719-STtofullyfund
  these four Purchase  Orders  and one other Purchase  Order  for bridge  maintenance  that was
  previously  approved  by the City  Council  on December  10, 2024.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The cumulative  total  required  for
the issuance  of Purchase  Orders  is $117,020,  which  will  be funded  from  the recommended
$200,000  appropriation  from  Proposition  C funds.  The Bridge  Maintenance  Services  Project  is
currently  budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year  2024/25  Capital  Improvement  Program  with  $125,000  in
Proposition  C funds.  To fully  fund  the project  and cover  anticipated  costs,  as well  as previous
expenditures,  staff recommends  an additional  appropriation  of $200,000  in Proposition  C funds.
A summary  table on the following  page outlines  the details  of the proposed  purchase  orders.

ANALYSIS:  The  City's  road  bridges  are in need  of general  maintenance  to preserve  their
structural  integrity  and ensure public  safety.  The Public  Works  Department  currently  lacks the in-
house  staffing  and  contracted  services  necessary  to  perform  this  work.  However,  the  City
maintains  an existing  contract  with  the  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Works
("LACDPW"),  which  offers  a range  of specialized  maintenance  programs.  Staff  recommends
utilizing  LACDPW's  services  to carry  out the needed  bridge  repairs.  This  approach  is consistent
with  prior  City  Council  actions-for  instance,  in 2015,  the Council  authorized  the use of County
services  for the design  and construction  of a curtain  wall  beneath  the Firestone  Boulevard  Bridge

  75
   at the Rio Hondo  Channel.

  County  services  offer  the following  advantages:

  *  Expertise  In-house  - County  has the expertise  to perform  the work  in-house,  through  the
  LACDPW.

  *  Cost Effectiveness  - The County  does not operate  for profit.  The City  will  reimburse  the
  County  for actual  repair  costs.

  *  Familiarity  -  The  County  is familiar  with  the design  of the Firestone  Bridge  and has
  performed  repair  work  of similar  nature  on many  occasions.

  *  Efficiency  - Utilizing  the County  for this work  avoids  the need to procure  professional
  design  services  to design  the repairs  and prepare  bid  documents  for  a design-bid-build
  process  that will  take many  months  to complete.

  LACDPW  has provided  cost estimates  for the necessary  bridge  maintenance  repairs.  City  staff has
  reviewed  these estimates  and determined  them to be reasonable.  The project  falls within  the scope
  of the existing  General  Services  Agreement  between  the City  of South  Gate  and Los Angeles
  County  and therefore  does not  require  a separate  Cooperative  Agreement.  A summary  of the
  service  requests  is provided  below.

  BACKGROUND:  The  City's  roadway  network  is supported  by  bridges  that  span  major
  infrastructure  such as freeways  and rivers.  Ownership  varies however  there are six bridges  owned
  by the City  for which  the city is responsible  for maintenance.

  LACDPW,  in conjunction  with  Caltrans,  performs  periodic  inspections  of the City's  bridges  and
  notifies  the City  of recommended  maintenance  through  Bridge  Inspection  Reports.  To date, the
  City  has budgeted  approximately  $625,000  for  bridge  maintenance  over  several  fiscal  years.
  However,  the project  has been delayed  due to the need to utilize  this  available  funding  for the
  Tweedy  Boulevard  Complete  Streets Project.  As part of this reprioritization  of funding,  $500,000
  in Proposition  C funds were reallocated  to support  Tweedy  improvements,  leaving  $125,000
  available for bridge maintenance.

  In collaboration  with  LACDPW,  City  staff developed  aphased  approach  to complete  the necessary
  bridge  repairs.  The project  was divided  into several  focused  areas, and individual  service  requests
  were  submitted  to the County  to initiate  engineering  and plaru'iing  work.  In response  to these
  service  requests,  the County  has provided  the City  with  multiple  fee proposals  totaling  $217,020

may  occur  and to provide  additional  funding  for project  management  services.

The County  has begun plaru'iing  efforts  on all of the above service  requests.  City Council  approval
will  allow  progress  to continue  in a coordinated  and timely  manner  on the repairs  for these bridges.

SUBJECT:  REALLOCATION  OF  PROPOSITION  C  FUNDS  TO  FULLY  FtJND
CONSTRUCTION  COMPLETION  OF  THE  GAJUFIELD  AVENUE  COMPLETE
STREET,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  564-ST

PURPOSE:  To authorize  the transfer  of Proposition  C funds, budgeted  in the Fiscal Year 2024/25
Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP"),  to fully  fund  services  rendered  for  the completion  of
construction  of the Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street Improvements  Project.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  authorizing  a $300,000  transfer
of Proposition  C Funds from the Southeast  Gateway  Line Light  Rail Project  to the Garfield  Avenue
Complete  Street Improvements,  City  Project  No. 564-ST,  to fully  fund  services  rendered  for the
completion  of construction.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The total  cost of implementing  the
Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street  Project  is  estimated  at $6.3  million.  The  recommended
allocation  of $300,000  in Proposition  C funds  will  ensure  the project  is fully  funded  and all
remaining  costs are covered.

ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street  Project  has been completed
and the project  is currently  in the close-out  phase.  As final  costs become  more  clearly  defined,
staff recommends  a transfer  of $300,000  to fully  fund  all remaining  project  expenses.  The project
was initially  anticipated  to be delivered  under budget,  which  allowed  for the reallocation  of over
$1 million  to support  otherhigh-priorityprojects  (most notably,  the Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets
Project).  Now  that  construction  is complete  and final  invoices  for  services  rendered  are being
submitted,  the recommended  $300,000  allocation  will  ensure  all outstanding  payments  are made
and remaining  close-out  activities  are fully  funded.

BACKGROUND:  Construction  of the Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street  Improvement  Project
has been successfully  completed.  This  transformative,  multi-million-dollar  capital  improvement
initiative  was  designed  to enhance  multimodal  transportation  options  and improve  safety  for
pedestrians  and  cyclists  along  Garfield  Avenue,  between  Firestone  Boulevard  and  Jefferson
Avenue.  The project  supports  the City's  long-term  vision  of creating  a safer, more accessible,  and
environmentally  sustainable  transportation  corridor.  It represents  a significant  milestone  in the

  94
 City's  ongoing  efforts  to modernize  its infrastructure  and deliver  a safer,  more  efficient,  and
visually  appealing  public  right-of-way  for all users.

The scope of work  included  a comprehensive  range of improvements  designed  to enhance  safety,
accessibility,  and sustainability  along the corridor.  Key elements  included  the installation  of raised
median  islands  with  drought-tolerant  landscaping  to improve  roadway  aesthetics  and reduce
vehicle  conflicts;  construction  ofADA-compliant  sidewalks  and curb ramps to ensure accessibility
for  all users;  and enhanced  midblock  crosswalks  with  pedestrian-activated  flashing  beacons  to
increase  visibility  and safety  at key crossing  points.  Additional  enhancements  included  upgraded
traffic  signals  and signage  to improve  traffic  flow  and compliance;  the addition  of dedicated  Class
II bike lanes to promote  safer cycling;  and stormwater  mitigation  features  integrated  withupgraded
irrigation  systems  to support  environmental  sustainability  and ease long-teri'n  maintenance.

The project  was funded  through  a combination  of local,  state, and federal  sources,  demonstrating
the  City's  effective  leveraging  of  diverse  funding  streams  to  support  vital  community
infrastructure.  Design  services  were  provided  by  Tetra  Tech,  with  construction  management
overseen  by Garu'iett Fleming.  The construction  contract  was awarded  to Sequel  Contractors,  Inc.,
who completed  the work  in accordance  with  all project  specifications  and timelines.

The  final  construction  cost is estimated  at $4,576,975.  The additional  $300,000  requested  will
ensure  all outstanding  project  expenses,  including  final  contractor  invoices  and associated  City
staff time,  are fully  funded.

The  project  is  currently  in  the  close-out  phase,  which  includes  processing  final  invoices,
completing  punch-list  items,  releasing  retention,  and preparing  final  documentation.

SUBJECT:  EXCESS  WORKERS'  COMPENSATION  INSURANCE  POLICY  WITH
SAFETY  NATIONAL  CASUALTY  CORPORATION

PURPOSE:  To renew  the City's  excess  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy  with  Safety
National  Casualty  Company  "Safety  National"  through  Alliant  Insurance  Services,  Incorporated
"Allignt",

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:
a.  Approve  an excess workers'  insurance  policy  with  Safety  National,  through  Alliant  for a
  one-year  term  cornmencing  July  1, 2025,  through  July  1, 2026,  with  a premium  in the
  amount  of $178,489.00.
b.  Authorize  payment  in the  amount  of $178,489.00  to Alliant  for  the policy  issued  by
  Safety  National.
C.  Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the "Request  to Bind  Coverage"  in a form  acceptable  to
  the City  Attorney.

FISCALIMPACT:  Funds,  in the  amount  of  $178,489.00  are included  in the  Fiscal  Year
2025/26  budget  for this  item  in Account  Number  511-220-12-6353  (Risk  Management  Fund  -
Insurance  Premiums).

ANALYSIS:  None.

BACKGRO{JND:  Each year, the City's  insurance  broker,  Alliant,  requests  quotes  on our excess
workers'  compensation  insurance  policy,  reviews  the proposals,  and assists the City  with  finding
the best  and most  cost-effective  coverage  to meet  our  needs.  For  the past  three  years,  staff
recommended  that the City  Council  renew  the excess  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy
with  Safety National  through  Alliant.

Only  one provider  submitted  a proposal  this year:  Safety  National  Casualty  Corporation  "Safety
National."  Safety  National  offered  very  competitive  Self-Insured  Retention  "SIR"  levels.  A
"SIR"  is an agreed-upon  dollar  amount  in the City's  workers'  compensation  insurance  policy  that
must  be paid  before  the insurer  is obligated  to pay  for  any remaining  workers'  compensation

  1

  96
 claims.  The proposed  SIR for this year's proposal  is $1,000,000  per police  officer  per Occurrence
(incident)  and $750,000  for all other employees  per occurrence  (incident).

Safety  National  decreased  its current  annual  premium  of $ 197,408.00  to $178,489  ($18,919
decrease),  nearly  an 1 1% decrease.  The proposed  premiiun  is based on the City's  loss history  and
"hard"  market  conditions,  as evidenced  by only  receiving  a single  proposal.  In addition,  the
proposed  premium  is based  on actual  and projected  City  payroll.  The Fiscal  Year  2024/25
projected  payroll  is  $34,720,554.  The  estimated  payroll  for  the  Fiscal  Year  2025/26  is
$35,762,170.61. This downward  trend  in the premium  (11%) reflects  the downward  trend  of the
City's  payroll  (-3%).

Per Alliant,  Safety  National  is an industry  Ieader  in workers'  compensation  insurance.  The City
has experienced  consistent  services  from  this provider  for the past four years.  Our 11%  decrease
in premiums  is primarily  due to a modest  decrease  in the City's  payroll.

Staff  is recommending  to renew  with  Safety  National.  Safety  National  considers  this  a premium
discount  for staying  with  them  as an existing  customer.

Flooding  is a serious threat to both personal and commercial  clients. Flooding  can happen anywhere,  not just  zone  referred  to as high-risk  areas
(Special  Flood Hazard Area). Your Alliant team is ready to explain how it works  and the associated costs.
Basic  Facts
Congress  created  the NFIP  in 1968  in response  to the rising  cost of taxpayer-funded  disaster  relief  for flood  victims  and the increasing  amount  of
damage  caused  by floods.  The NFIP  makes  federally  backed  flood  insurance  available  in communities  that agree  to adopt  and enforce  floodplain
management  ordinances  to reduce  future  flood  damage.  The NFIP  is self-supporting  for the average  historical  loss year.  This  means  that  unless
there  is a widespread  disaster,  operating  expenses  and flood  insurance  claims  are financed  through  premiums  collected.

Commercial  buildings  or residential  dwellings  owned  by commercial  entities  are considered  commercial  property.  All others  are residential  dwellings

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  receiving  and filing  the FY 2025-

ANALYSIS:  At tonight's  meeting,  the first  of three scheduled  budget  sessions,  staff will  provide
a comprehensive  ovetaview  of the  Proposed  Budget  for  Fiscal  Year  2025-26.  Following  tl'iis
overview,  departments  will  present  detailed  budgets  during  subsequent  meetings,  highlighting
their  core services,  notable  changes,  initiatives,  goals,  and objectives.  On June 24, 2025,  the City
Council  will  consider  adopting  a  resolution  to  formally  approve  the  Proposed  Budget,
incorporating  any adjustments  discussed  during  these sessions.  These  meetings  are open to the
public,  offering  opportunities  for community  paiticipation  through  public  comments.

Tlie Proposed  Budget  document  is currently  being  finalized  and will  be available  in dra:it form  to
the City Council  and tlie public  via the City's  webpage  no later than June 12, 2025. The preparation
of this year's  budget  document  has required  additional  time  due to significant  transitions  within
the Administrative  Services  Depaitment,  including  the departure  of the previous  Administrative
Services  Director  and Deputy  Director  as well  as the subsequent  transition  from  an interim  to  a

new  permanent  Administrative  Services  Director.  The  finance  team  has worked  diligently  to
ensure the accuracy  and completeness  of tlie budget  document,  managing  a substantial  workload
that included  addressing  extensive  accounting  tasks and executing  a significant  mid-year  budget
adjustment  recently  approved  by the City  Council.  Staff  anticipates  several  adjustments  to the
budget  following  departmental  and  City  Council  reviews.  These  adjustments  will  be clearly
tracked  and reported  in a dedicated  exhibit  attached  to the resolution,  ensuring  full  transparency
and accountability.

It is critical  to understand  that the budget  is a dynamic  plan,  adaptable  to emerging  needs and
circumstances  throughout  tlie fiscal  year.  Regular  budget  updates,  including  a mid-year  review,
will  provide  opportunities  for  necessary  adjustments  and  serve  as a platform  for  initiating
discussions  about potential  themes  and priorities  for subsequent  fiscal  years.

 The City  is entering  FY  2025-26  facing  significant  fiscal  challenges.  Chief  among  tliese  is an
ongoing  structural  deficit,  primarily  driven  by external  cost pressures  largely  beyond  orir control,
including  escalating  pension  obligations,  CalPERS  investment  volatility,  and rising  insurance
premiums  for  workers'  compensation  and general  liability  coverage.  Additionally,  contracted
medical  coverage  through  CalPERS  continues  to experience  significant  cost increases,  alongside
broader  inflationary  pressures  affecting  virtually  all operational  expenses.  Political  uncertainty  at
state  and  federal  levels,  including  fluctuating  tariffs  and  shifting  economic  policies,  fuither
complicates  the  financial  landscape  for  local  governments.  Given  these  constraints  and the
inherently  limited  funding  mechanisms  available  to cities-primarily  property  and sales taxes-it
is essential  for South  Gate to actively  identify  and maximize  all feasible  revenue  oppoitunities.
This approach  will  lielp  ensure the City's  long-term  financial  sustainability,  supporting  our ability
to maintain  essential  community  services  and  address  critical  infrastructure  needs,  such  as
addressing  aging  infrastructure  and replacing  the  City's  Enterprise  Resource  Plaru'iing  (ERP)
system.  As  we  confront  these  challenges,  the  City  Council  will  undoubtedly  face  difficult
decisions.  Staff  is fully  committed  to suppoiting  the Council's  direction  and ensuring  that any
policy  changes  are  implemented  fairly,  transparently,  and witli  the long-term  interests  of the entire
community  in  mind.

BACKGROUND:  A municipal  budget  addresses  city policies,  city operations  and communicates
the anticipated  financial  activities  to botli the public  and legislative  bodies  of tlie impacted  entities.
The following  two  meetings  will  be to review  the various  proposed  departmental  projects.  The
City  Council  will  be asked to consider  approving  a Resolution  to adopt  the Proposed  Budget  for
Fiscal  Year 2024-25  on June 24, 2025.

Goveri'u'nent  Code  Section  53901  requires  each local  agency  to file  its budget  with  the county
auditor  within  60 days after the beginning  of its fiscal  year. If an agency  does not have a "formal
budget",  it must file a listing  of its anticipated  revenues  togetlier  with  its expenditures  for the fiscal
year in progress.  Staff anticipates  that tlie Proposed  Budget  for Fiscal  Year 2025-26  will  be adopted
on  June 24, 2025,  which  is within  the timeframe  for submitting  the budget  to the county  auditor.

Additionally,  each year, the City must adopt an appropriation  limit  called  the Gann limit.  The Gann
limit  is designed  to limit  the amount  of revenue  that can be appropriated  in a fiscal  year.  The
appropriations  subject  to the limit  are those that expend proceeds  of taxes (e.g., Property  Tax, Sales
Tax,  and Transient  Occupancy  Tax)  less any exclusion  for qualified  capital  outlay,  debt service,
and federal  mandates.  Tlie finance  staff will  be calculating  the Gann Limit  for FY 2025-26.

minutes_text:
CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  JUNE  10, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  7:02 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City
  Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  Mario  Dominguez  is requesting  the City  Council  place an item on the
  agenda to change  the email  fees, having  to do with  public  records  request,
  specifically  Fair Political  Practices  Commission  (FPPC).

  Lizette  Ruiz,  Kauffman  Ave, thanked  the City  Council  for speaking  out
  and being  involved  in meetings  with  different  government  officials  form
  the state regarding  the ICE raids.  She also believes  the budget  item should
  have been heard earlier  in the meeting.

  Francisco  Gallegos,  Otis Street,  is concerned  about the illegal  fireworks  in
  this community.

  Rubin  Pichardo,  long-time  South  Gate resident,  is present  tonight  to
  clarify  certain  comments  made by Vice Mayor  Barron.

  Javier,  South  Gate resident,  is asking  for clarification  on the city's  stance
  regarding  ICE.

  Osvaldo  Pichardo,  San Gabriel  Ave, is present  tonight  to clarify  cornrnents
  made by Vice  Mayor  Barron  and Council  Member  Hurtado.

  Alice,  South  Gate resident,  is concerned  that people  show up at Council
  Meetings  and are accusing  the current  City  Council  Members  of fraud.
  Her complaint  is with  the Parks Department  because  she cannot  attend  the
  weight  control  meetings  because  they are only  in Spanish.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  CONT'D  Cecilia  Caballero,  South  Gate resident,  owns  a company  for multilingual
  books  for children.  She mentioned  a literacy  festival  for this summer.  She

  received  a call from  a good friend  that was planning  a pride  festival  but

  got turned  down.  She's present  tonight  supporting  him.

  Adolfo  Varas,  South  Gate resident,  was a keynote  speaker  at a graduation
  in the City of Bell. He stated it took him five years to advocate for his
  LGBTQ+  community  to declare the month of June as Pride Month. He
  stated establishing  a Pride Festival  that shows  unity,  love,  education,  and

  resources.  He thanked  Councilwoman  Avalos  and every  elected  official

  throughout  the southeast  Los Angeles  region,  multiple  different  cities

  reaching  out, wanting  his Pride  Festival.  He hopes the City  Clerk  will  read

  the emails  and not give a summary.  He is asking  the City  Council  to

  continue  supporting  the LGBTQ+  community.

  Laura  thanked  everyone  for their  support.  She is the Membership  Director

  for the City  of Bell  Chamber  of Commerce.  She stated the Pride  Festival  is

  to provide  resources  for the youth  that do not have anywhere  to go.

  Vince,  SELA  Pride  Festiva  Chair,  and resident  of the cities  of San Pedro

  and Paramount.  He stated his first Pride Festival  was hosted  in the City  of

  South  Gate.

  Miguel  Angel  Alvarez  Godinez,  LA County  Commissioner  on HIV,  and is

  present  tonight  in support  of the SELA  Pride  Festival.  He would  like this
  city to support  its citizens.

  Ezequiel  Flores,  South  Gate resident,  and reiterated  what his other
  colleagues  have stated.

EMAILS  Ed Rod expressing  disappointment  with  the City  of South  Gate's  decision

  to withdraw  from  participating  in the SELA  Pride.  He is urging  the city to

  consider  its decision,  stating  that pulling  back sends a harmful  message,
  especially  to the youth.

  Tenaya,  South  Gate resident  and SELA  Pride  attendee,  is expressing
  concern  about the city's  recent  decision  to withdraw  from  hosting  this

  year's  pride  She emphasized
  event.  South  Gate needs pride  celebration  to

  support  its peer residents and allies.

  Sophie  Ryan,  South  Gate resident,  expresses  appreciation  for the city's

  ongoing  efforts  to be a safe and inclusive  space and special  thanks  to Mr.

  Costley  for his long-standing  support  and student  events  over the past
  decades.  Ms. Ryan is asking Council to review  the proposal  and consider
  the possibility of hosting the event this summer.

  Page 2 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGF.NDA

ITEMS)  CONT'D  EMAILS  Miss Ady  Cortez  in response  to a social  media  post by Adolfo  Varas
  regarding  the city's  involvement  in the SELA  Pride Festival.  She states
  that one of Mr. Vara's  staff members  dropped  off the event application  on
  Wednesday,  June 4'h and later reviewed  and corrected  by her mother
  before  being  submitted  on Thursday,  June 5fll. She added that he had
  previously  been informed  that the application  should  have been submitted
  3 to 6 months  prior  to the event.  She concluded  by saying  it is unfair  to
  spread misinformation  and that doing  so reflects  poorly  on the LGBTQ
  community.

  Miss  Jennifer  Daly,  on behalf  of Ruben  Pichardo  and several  concerned
  residents  regarding  the city's  code enforcement  practices,  alleging  that
  South  Gate residents  are being  unfairly  cited for minor  or unfounded
  violations  while  large commercial  entities  are allowed  to operate  without
  proper  permits  or enforcement.

  Miss  Martha  Torres,  Community  Engagement  Liaison  with  the Fair
  Housing  Foundation,  informing  the city about the free services  the
  organization  provides  to South  Gate residents.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  stated that regarding  the city's  support  of
  pride  community  and Pride Festival,  the city has a history  from  both City
  Council  and staff to support  the cornrnunity  and has had past pride
  festivals.  He stated the city has a set of rules and regulations  to make sure
  all the community  members  want to do events  in the park.

  Mayor  Davila  stated the City  of South  Gate was the first to have the Pride
  Festival  during  Covid.  She stated there is a process  and regulations  that
  need to be followed.

  Mayor  Davila  stated she has LGBTQ  family  members  and is a big
  supporter  of the LGBTQ  community.  She also informed  the public  that the
  Proclamation  for Pride  Month  is at the next Council  Meeting.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works,  reported  construction  on the
  residential  resurfacing  project.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  stated the park is very
  busy. He mentioned  the registration  for classes has started  for the summer
  quarter.

  Gabriel  Perez, Director  of Community  Development,  stated staff is
  working  on a fagade  improvement  program  for Tweedy  Boulevard.

  Page 3 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

REPORTS  AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  stated that for a couple
  of meetings  we have had technical  issues with  the streaming  services.

  Staff take this very  seriously  and have resources  that have been dedicated
  to troubleshooting  and ensuring  the connection  was stable.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  has nothing  to report.  He

  wished  everybody  Happy  Father's  Day.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Chief  of Police,  stated there isn't  a real solution  to the

  fireworks.  He agrees staff is an issue. He mentioned  the citation  fees. He

  mentioned  the street fair was well attended without  any issues.

  The Chief  was on a conference call regarding  irnrnigration  with the LAPD

  Chief and Sheriff with the 45 Police Chiefs about what we are doing
  locally within the communities.  He has a profound  respect for the law. It is
  agreed in law enforcement  that there is a big gap in communication  with

  the federal govemment.  The Chief stated that the federal government  does

  not need anyone's permission  to come into the community.  There  is no

  mandate  that they community  with  the cities.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  stated everyone  has the right  for peaceful

  protesting  that's  encouraged  in our democratic  society  and supported  by

  the police,  council  and staff. But if the protesting  creates vandalism  or

  aggression  that will be addressed  like any  other  law.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney  had nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  will  save his time on the proposed  budget

  item.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  spoke on the summarized  email  comments.  She

  also spoke on the fee resolution Mr. Dominguez  brought  up. She wished
  everybody  a Happy Father's Day.

  Council  Member  Avalos  thanked  the cornrnunity  and appreciated  the

  compliments  by the Pichardo  family.  She acknowledges  the South Gate

  families  that are afraid  to leave their homes,  go to work,  take their children

  to school  or the park. She's made a few social  media  posts if anyone  needs

  resources, to reach out to her.

  Council  Member  Avalos  attended  the Southeast  Water  Coalition  and on

  April  9fh it was indicated  the water  rates were going  to increase  by 4%.

  The Budget  Advisory  Committee  indicated  that it was not needed. The
  water increased  by 3.8. She also attended  the Men's Health, but a lot of the
  community  leaders did not attend, and she understands  the reason.  She

  wished  all the fathers  a Happy  Father's  Day.

  Page 4 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member  Avalos  is concerned  and disappointment  regarding
  Council  Member  Hurtado's  comtnents  referring  to a colleague.  She is
  demanding  this Council  act through  censure  or mandatory  training.  She is
  asking  for a public  apology.  Since she got on Council,  she has never
  spoken  ill will of anyone in public  because  she holds  herself  at a higher
  standard.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated that he never  said any profanity  about  any
  colleague.  At the request  of Mr. Pichardo,  Council  Member  Hurtado
  visited  him over a code enforcement  issue. He informed  Mr. Pichardo  that
  he was not ready to make any decision  as to whether  Mr. Pichardo  got
  cited properly  or not. He would  forward  it to the City  Manager  for his
  review.  Mr. Pichardo  never  asked Council  Member  Hurtado  for anything.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated attending  a training  session  at the
  Western  States Carpenters  Union.  He attended  Cal State Dominguez  in
  2017 and 2019 to get a degree  and one of the courses  he took  was Queer
  Studies.  He had a nephew  that was part of the LGBTQ  community.  He and
  his colleagues  have always  been respectful  and supportive  of the LGBTQ
  community  events.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated attending  meetings  with  local  leaders
  from  the southeast  area regarding  the ICE issues. He asked the public  to be
  careful  what is posted  on social  media.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  everyone  present  tonight.  He supports  the
  LGBTQ  community  and understands  the firework  issues. He attended  the
  Men's  Health  fair. He stated that the natives  of this country  are the
  American  Indians.  Everyone  else came from  somewhere.  It is okay to
  protest,  but peacefully.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked if the firework  fees can be increased  to deter the
  use of them.

  Chief  Arakawa  responded  that it's City  Councils  decision.  The fines  are
  high already.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  is willing  to discuss  increasing  the firework  fees.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated many  cannot  pay the fines  or it gets appealed.  The
  first  start would  be to ban fireworks.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  questioned  the reason the SWAT  truck  during  the
  street fair.

  Page 5 of 8
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JUNE  10, 2025

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Chief  Arakawa  stated the SWAT  truck  would  be driving  through  the alleys,
  and it is taken out to cornrnunity events. The SWAT  truck  is a military
  vehicle. ICE does not drive military  vehicles.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  stated they need to be the eyes to be able to inform the
  residents  of what's  going on. The news will show violence, fires but not
  peace'ful  protests.  He attended  meetings  with  local  leaders  regarding  ICE
  ISSueS.

  Mayor  Davila  attended  several  graduations,  the Centennial  Celebration  for
  San Gabriel  Avenue,  Victoria  Elementary  School  and ribbon  cutting  for
  the Tweedy  Boulevard.

  Mayor  Davila  spoke on the ICE issues and the resources.

  The City  Council  recessed  at 8:45 p.m.,  and reconvened  at 8:53 p.m.,  with
RECESS

  all Members  of Council  present.

DEVIATE  FROM

THE  AGENDA  At this time,  there being  no objections,  Mayor  Davila  stated that item  6
  would  be considered  out of its regular  agenda  order.

6
